questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When synapsis is complete all along the chromosome, the cell is said to have entered a stage called
questions.solution: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes during the zygotene stage of meiosis. Each pair is called bivalent. One chromosome of the pair comes from the male parent and other from the female parent. Each member of the pair is of the same length, their centromeres are in the same position and they usually have the same number of genes arranged in the same order. After zygotene stage, cell enters in pachytene stage in which the bivalents become spiralled, shortened and thickened.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During cell growth, DNA synthesis takes place in
questions.solution: DNA replication occurs in the S phase of the cell cycle. S phase, or synthesis, is the phase of the cell cycle when DNA packaged into chromosomes is replicated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Spindle fibres attach on to:
questions.solution: Kinetochore of chromosomes facilitates the attachment of spindle fibre (chromosomal fibre) and the poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The diagram below shows a cell cycle.



Which of the following process occur during V?
options: Chromosomes condense and become shorter and thicker
High metabolic rate and synthesis of proteins and cellular organelles
questions.solution: In the given diagram, the 'V' labeled phase is the G<sub>1</sub> phase. G<sub>1</sub> phase marks the start of interphase. G<sub>1</sub> phase is the metabolically active phase and during this phase, the cell grows in size. Synthesis of mRNA and protein of DNA synthesis occurs in this phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a cell, the number of chromosomes is the same, but the amount of DNA content has changed from C to 2C. Also, the amount of histones in the cell becomes double. In which stage of the cell cycle, this process could have happened?
questions.solution: G<sub>1</sub> phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During G<sub>1</sub> phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA and histones per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as C then it increases to 2C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G<sub>1</sub>, even after the S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In an organism, if the normal diploid number of chromosomes is 8, how many chromatids are present in each daughter cell at the end of meiosis I
questions.solution: Meiosis I ends when the chromosomes of each homologous pair arrive at opposing poles of the cell. The microtubules disintegrate, and a new nuclear membrane forms around each haploid set of chromosomes. The chromosomes uncoil, forming chromatin again, and cytokinesis occurs, forming two non-identical daughter cells. A resting phase known as interkinesis or interphase II happens in some organisms. Therefore, each daughter cell will have 4 chromosomes and 8 chromatids, at the end of the meiosis I.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If radioactive thymidine is used during S-phase of interphase, which part of the chromosome will become radioactive?
questions.solution:
The replication of genetic material during cell division takes place in S-phase. The complete genetic material is replication thus euchromatin as well as heterochromatin both are replicated. Though euchromatin replicates in early S-phase while 
heterochromatin replicates in late S-phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the meiosis type of cell division, the centromere divides during which stage?
questions.solution: Anaphase II is the stage when sister chromatids of every chromosome separate and begin to move towards the opposite ends of the cell. Splitting of centromere occurs in this stage. The separation and the movement are due to the shortening of the kinetochore microtubules. Anaphase II precedes telophase II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the given statements are incorrect?

A. Nucleolus and nuclear membrane disappear in prophase.
B. Synaptonemal complex formation occurs during zygotene.
C. The enzyme responsible for crossing over in pachytene is recombinase.
D. Chiasmata formation occurs in diakinesis.
questions.solution: Nucleolus and nuclear membrane disappear during prophase and reappears during telophase of cell division. Synaptonemal complex is a protein network that holds two chromosomes of a bivalent formed during synapsis in the zygotene of prophase I of meiosis. Chiasmata formation arises during diplotene stage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The figure given below represents the stage of cell division. Read the following statements.



(i) Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER reform.
(ii) Chromatids move to the opposite pole.
(iii) The activity of the recombinase enzyme.
(iv) Homologous chromosomes separate while sister chromatids associated at their centromere.
(v) Initiation of the assembly of the mitotic spindle.

How many of the above statements is not true with respect to the above figure?
questions.solution: The above diagram is of anaphase of mitosis. During anaphase of mitosis, sister chromatids of chromosome move to their respective pole. Thus, only statement ii is correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally. Such cells are said to be in
questions.solution: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally, as needed to replace cells that have been lost because of injury or cell death. These cells do not divide further exit G<sub>1</sub> phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G<sub>0</sub>) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All the following statements are correct, except
options: Interphase is the shortest period of cell cycle
Cell growth, in terms of cytoplasmic increase, is a continuous process
Cycles of growth and division allow a single cell to form a structure consisting of millions of cell
The replicated DNA are distributed to daughter nuclei by a complex series of events during cell division.
questions.solution: Interphase is the phase of the cell cycle in which the cell spends and performs the majority of its time. Then, in preparation for cellular division, it increases in size. Mitosis (nuclear division) is the most dramatic stage of the cell cycle, involving a major reorganisation of virtually all components of the cell. During mitosis (Nuclear Division) the chromosome condense, the nuclear envelope of most cells break down, the cytoskeleton reorganise to form the mitotic spindle and the chromosome move to opposite pole.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Meiosis-I is also called as heterotypic division/reductional cell division. Select the correct option by comparing the phase of the meiosis and their respective events from lists I and II.
 
 List I
(Phase of meiosis)		  List II
(Event that occurs)
1. Prophase I  Crossing over occurs
2. Metaphase I  Sister chromatids migrate to opposite poles
3. Anaphase I  Homologous chromosomes line up at equator in pairs
questions.solution: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes which occurs during prophase I of meiosis during a process called a synopsis. During metaphase, the homologous chromosomes line up at the equator in pairs and in anaphase, the sister chromatids migrate towards opposite poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
For the stages of the cell cycle, select the correct option.

A. A chromosome is arranged at the equator - Metaphase.
B. Centromere splits and chromatids are separated - Anaphase I.
C. The pairing between homologous chromosomes takes place - Zygotene.
questions.solution: During metaphase chromosome are arranged at equator to form metaphasic plate and spindle fibre attaches to kinetochore of centromere. Splitting of centromere and separation of chromatids occurs during anaphase of mitosis and Anaphase II of meiosis. In Anaphase I chromosomal pairs separates and this is known as  disjunction. Pairing of homologous chromosome occurs during zygotene and is known as synapsis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Spindle fibres are made up of
questions.solution: Spindle fiber ​is the assembly of the mitotic spindle, the microtubules, the proteinaceous components of the cell cytoplasm help in the process of cell division and are made of a protein called tubulin. The spindle is necessary to equally divide the chromosomes in a parental cell into two daughter cells during both types of nuclear division: mitosis and meiosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In meiosis, division is
questions.solution: Meiotic division occurs in two stages, meiosis I and meiosis II, dividing the cells once at each stage. Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes, producing two haploid cells (N chromosomes, 23 in humans), and thus meiosis I is referred to as a reductional division. In meiosis II, an equational division similar to mitosis will occur whereby the sister chromatids are finally split, creating a total of 4 haploid cells (23 chromosomes, N) - two from each daughter cell from the first division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The nuclear membrane disappears in
questions.solution: During early prophase, the chromatin network condenses and resolves into a definite number of chromosomes. In late prophase, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus begin to disappear. The daughter centrioles (in animal cells) start moving away from each other, till they occupy a polar position.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Analyze the events occurring during every stage of the cell cycle, how the amount of DNA content <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>)</mo></math> per cell changes and select the correct option.
options: DNA content becomes doubled during S phase of cell cycle
DNA content is reduced to half during anaphase
DNA content remain same during meiosis I
questions.solution:
Synthesis of DNA occurs by DNA replication and the amount of DNA per cell doubles (C becomes 2C). It is important to note that in spite of the doubling DNA, chromosome number remains the same. 

(ii) During anaphase as the division of centromere takes place, the chromatids move to the opposite poles, causing the DNA content to become half (from 2C to C), however, the number of chromosomes remains the same.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Two features present in meiosis but absent in mitosis are
options: Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between them
questions.solution: Homologous chromosomes are made up of chromosome pairs of approximately the same length, centromere position, and staining pattern, for genes with the same corresponding loci. One homologous chromosome is inherited from the organism's mother; the other is inherited from the organism's father. They have a tendency to pair with each other during meiosis and undergoes crossing over to produce new genetic recombinations.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The phase in which both the chromosome and DNA content becomes half is
questions.solution: During anaphase I the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres. As a result, this stage is called the reductional division stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: DNA replication occurs during
questions.solution: The S phase of the cell cycle is the period for DNA replication. This is the period where duplication of genetic material takes place. This is one of the preparatory periods before mitosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: At G<sub>1</sub> stage, which phenomenon takes place
questions.solution:
At the G1 phase, the RNA and protein are synthesized.
The G1 phase, or Gap 1 phase, is the first of four phases of the cell cycle that takes place in eukaryotic cell division. In this part of interphase, the cell synthesizes mRNA and proteins in preparation for subsequent steps leading to mitosis. G1 phase ends when the cell moves into the S phase of interphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out the number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA in a spore mother cell of Bryophytes in G<sub>2</sub> stage (If the spore contains 5 chromosomes and 5pg of DNA) -
questions.solution: Spore mother cell is diploid and spore is haploid. If spore has 5 chromosomes and 5pg DNA than the spore mother cell has 10 chromosomes and 10pg DNA in the G<sub>1</sub> phase. Since DNA replication occurs during S phase but chromosome number remains unchanged. Thus chromosome in the G<sub>2</sub> phase is 10 and the quantity of DNA is 20 pg.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect for the interphase stage?
options: It covers over 95% of the total duration of cell cycle
questions.solution: Replication of DNA occurs during S-Phase of interphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following structures is not common to mitotic cells of higher plants?
questions.solution: Plants cells do not have centrioles. Cell plate appears during cytokinesis in dividing cells. Centromere holds the sister chromatids in a chromosome. Spindle fibres appear during metaphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Crossing over in diploid organism is responsible for
questions.solution: Crossing over involves physical exchange of genetic material between non sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes and leads to recombination.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: To study any kind of genetic abnormality arising due to change is chromosome number, the karyotype is prepared. Which of the following stages is most suitable to develop a karyotype?
questions.solution: A karyotype is a profile of organisms chromosomes that are organized by their size, pattern, and location of centromere. Chromosomes are most distinct in the metaphase stage. In the telophase stage, they regain their coiled composition. In anaphase, the chromatids separate and move towards opposite poles. In the prophase stage, the chromosomes appear thread-like and individual chromatids cannot be seen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The two chromatids of a metaphase chromosome represent
options: Replicated chromosomes to be separated at anaphase
Homologous chromosomes of a diploid set
Non-homologous chromosomes joined at the centromere
Maternal and paternal chromosomes joined at the centromere
questions.solution: The two chromatids of a metaphase chromosome represent replicated chromosomes, arranged at the equatorial plane of the cell, to be separated at anaphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The X-shaped structures formed during the largest stage of meiosis-I are called
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: The beginning of diplotene is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures are called chiasmata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Disjunction is:
questions.solution: Normal separation of chromosomes towards the opposite poles during anaphase-I of cell division is called a disjunction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the organisms show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells?
questions.solution: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cells. The plants show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells and show alternation of generations.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The spindle fibres are made up of _______ protein.
questions.solution:
Spindle fibres are formed of microtubules, which play an important role in movement of chromosomes and centrioles during cell division. Biochemically a profilament of microtubule is made of a protein called tubulin. Tubulin is an acidic protein, which occurs in two different forms called α -tubulin and β -tubulin. Cytoplasmic microtubules are highly dynamic structures constantly forming and dis-appearing depending on cell activities.

Myosin is fibrous functional protein of muscle. Myoglobin protein of muscle cells act as a reservoir of oxygen. Albumin is the smallest and most numerous proteins in the blood which are involved in cargo of toxic materials.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell undergoes mitosis in 30 minutes. Find the number of cells produced after 24 hours if initially 10⁵ cells are present.
questions.solution: A cell undergoes one round of mitosis in 30 minutes; thus, it undergoes 48 divisions in 24 hours. Hence, the number of cells produced is <math><msup><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>48</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Each cell undergoes division, so the total number of cells produced is <math><msup><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>48 </mn></mrow></msup><mo>× </mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The bacterial cell divides in every minute. If it takes one hour to fill up a cup, how much time will be taken to fill half the cup?
questions.solution: The number of bacteria becomes double after each division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A diploid living organism develops from zygote by which type of the following repeated cell divisions?
questions.solution: The zygote is formed by the fusion of male and female gametes. Hence a zygote is diploid in nature. The male and female gametes are formed by meiosis in a diploid organism. A diploid living organism develops from zygote by repeated mitotic divisions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tubulin protein is synthesized in which phase of cell cycle?
questions.solution: Interphase is the portion of the cell cycle that is not accompanied by observable changes under the microscope and includes the <math><msub><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>, S and <math><msub><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> phases. During interphase, the cell grows <math><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></math>, replicates its DNA (S) and prepares for mitosis <math><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></math>.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the phase 'C' of the cell cycle given below.
questions.solution: A nuclear envelope forms around each set of chromosomes, and cytokinesis occurs producing four daughter cells, each with a haploid set of chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Splitting of centromere of a chromosome during cell division occurs in
questions.solution: During cell division, when chromosomes are pulled apart into different cells, the centromeres present in the middle of a chromosomes split. This splitting of chromosome occurs during anaphase of mitosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: At the beginning of the final stage of mitosis,
options: The chromosomes that have reached their respective poles decondense.
Nuclear envelope assembles around the chromosome clusters.
Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements.
Nucleolus, golgi complex and ER reform.
questions.solution: At the beginning of the final stage of mitosis, i.e., telophase, the chromosomes that have reached their respective poles decondense and lose their individuality. The individual chromosomes can no longer be seen and chromatin material tends to collect in a mass in the two poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Synaptonemal complex is formed during
questions.solution: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. Such paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. Electron micrographs of this stage indicate that chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called the synaptonemal complex. It forms the structural basis for pairing and synapsis of meiotic chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following phases do not take place in a cell exhibiting a syncytium?
questions.solution: In some organisms, karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (eg. liquid endosperm in coconut).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A number of bivalents are 8 in prophase I. What will be the number of chromosomes during anaphase II?
questions.solution: At prophase I the number of bivalents is 8, i.e., 2n = 16. Thus, after meiosis I, the daughter cell would have 16/2 = 8 chromosomes. Therefore, the number of the chromosome at anaphase II will be 8.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In meiosis crossing over is initiated at
questions.solution: Pachytene is the third stage of the prophase of meiosis, following zygotene, during which the paired chromosomes shorten and thicken, the two chromatids of each separate, and exchange of segments between chromatids occurs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mitotic anaphase differs from metaphase in possessing
options: Same number of chromosomes and same number of chromatids
Half number of chromosomes and half number of chromatids
Half number of chromosomes and same number of chromatids
Same number of chromosomes and half number of chromatids
questions.solution: In mitotic anaphase, the sister chromatids separate from each other and begin to move towards the opposite poles. Hence, the number of chromosomes remains the same but the amount of DNA or chromatids becomes half.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out the incorrect match with respect to the given diagram.
questions.solution:
'A' represents spindle fibre, not kinetochore. (kinetochore is the protein structure on centromere where the spindle fibres attach during cell division to pull sister chromatids apart.)

'D' represents centromere.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Separation of the homologous chromosome of a pair occurs during
questions.solution: Separation of homologous chromosome of a pair occurs during anaphase I of meiosis I, and this is called disjunction. It results in reduction in chromosome number to half.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The points at which crossing over has taken place between homologous chromosomes are called
questions.solution: The separation of the homologous chromosomes is not completed in deplotene stage. They remain attached at one or more points where crossing over has occurred. These points of attachment are called as chiasmata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In mitosis, the centromeres split and chromatids separate during:
questions.solution: In anaphase, the kinetochore are pulled apart, centromere splits and chromatids are separated, which starts moving towards the opposite poles. This results in a reduction in the quantity of DNA to half which is replicated during the S phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which stage of prophase-I recombination nodules appear in meiosis?
questions.solution: The first two stages of prophase-I are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage that is pachytene. During this stage, bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads. This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about metaphase-I?
options: Spindle fibers are attached at chromomere
questions.solution:
During the prophase of meiosis I, homologous chromosomes pair and form synapses. The paired chromosomes are called bivalents. The bivalent has two chromosomes and four chromatids, with one chromosome coming from each parent. The bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate
during metaphase I. The microtubules from the opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochore of homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: 'Endomitosis' refers to
options: Division of nucleus without chromosomal division
Division of chromosome without nuclear division
questions.solution: 'Endomitosis' refers to the replication of DNA without any nuclear division. In this process, the division of chromosomes will be seen without nuclear division and resulting in an increased number of chromosomes in the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cell division or mitosis is a normal process in a living cell, but sudden and abnormal mitosis in an organ will frequently result in a
questions.solution: The cancer cells multiply by abnormal rapid and uncontrolled mitosis. Cancer is caused due to uncontrolled growth of the cells and forms from the extra mass tissue known as tumour. Generally, cancer is defined as uncontrolled proliferation of cells without any differentiation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During embryonic development, the total cell cycle time for a given cell type can change. These changes are primarily due to variation in
questions.solution: The division cycle of most cells consists of four coordinated processes: cell growth, DNA replication, distribution of the duplicated chromosomes to daughter cells, and cell division. During G<sub>1</sub>, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. G<sub>1</sub> phase is the most variable phase of the cell cycle as far as the duration of the phase is concerned. It is the longest phase of interphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which stage of prophase I of meiosis lasts for many days?
questions.solution: During meiosis in animals, cell gets arrested in Diplotene, and this is of longest duration. In egg laying birds, maximum yolk proteins are synthesized during diplotene stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The intrameiotic interphase is called:
questions.solution: The stage between two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis. It is generally short-lived and is followed by prophase-II, much simpler prophase than prophase-I of meiosis-I.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the correct answer regarding the phase of meiosis and their respective events using the lists given below:
 
 
  List I
(Phase of meiosis)		 List II
(Event over occurs)
 (1)  Prophase I  Crossing over occurs
 (2)  Metaphase II  Sister chromatids migrate to opposite poles
 (3)  Anaphase I  Homologous line up at equator in pairs
questions.solution: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes, which occurs during prophase I of meiosis and is called synapsis. The homologous chromosomes line at equator in pairs during metaphase I and the sister chromatids migrate towards opposite poles during anaphase I.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How is the DNA of the cell affected during S-phase of the cell cycle?
options: DNA amount per cell is doubled
DNA amount per cell is halved
DNA amount per cell is tripled
DNA amount per cell remains the same
questions.solution: The interphase of the cell cycle is divided into G<sub>1</sub>, S and G<sub>2</sub> phases. During the S phase or synthesis phase in the cell cycle, the DNA undergoes replication. Thus, the DNA is duplicated and quantity is doubled.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When synapsis is completed all along the chromosome, the cell is said to have entered a stage called
questions.solution: Synapsis or syndesis is the process of pairing of homologous chromosome to form bivalent, it occurs during zygotene of prophase I of meiosis. After completion of pairing the cell enter Pachytene where crossing over occurs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If the number of bivalents is 10 in prophase - I, what will be the number of the chromosomes during late anaphase - II in each cell?
questions.solution: Cell with 10 bivalents consists of 20 chromosomes, thus during anaphase I disjunction of chromosomes results in reduction of chromosome number to half as a result each cell after meiosis I will have 10 chromosomes. During anaphase II centromere splits and chromatids are separated. Thus at the end of anaphase II each cell consists of 10 chromosome with one chromatid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: For successful cell replacement during tissue repair, the chromosome content of each daughter cell must be identical to that of the mother cell. Which stages of mitosis make sure that each daughter cell receives one chromatid from each chromatid pair?
questions.solution: Metaphase in mitosis ensure the orientation of chromatid pair in proper alignment assisted by the centrioles and microtubules. Anaphase is the stage where the chromatids are separated at centromere to ensure each new cell that form gets equal number of chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of these events are parts of mitosis?

I. Interphase
II. Anaphase
III. Cytokinesis
questions.solution: Mitosis is one of the two divisional phase in cell-cycle. It occurs after interphase and is succeeded by cytokinesis (cytoplasm division). Mitosis has prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase as the stages of karyokinesis in the same order.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: From the following, the correct appearance of a chromosome at the beginning of prophase of mitosis and the number of DNA strands in the chromosome is:
options: Appearance of one chromosome: , Number of DNA strands: 2
Appearance of one chromosome: , Number of DNA strands: 4
Appearance of one chromosome: , Number of DNA strands: 1
Appearance of one chromosome: , Number of DNA strands: 2
questions.solution: In mitosis, before entering the divisional phase, cell has undergone the S-phase where DNA duplication occurs resulting in formation and appearance of chromosome where each chromosome has two sister chromatids joined and each chromatid has 2 DNA. So in total 4 DNA in the chromosome during prophase of mitosis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these stages of mitosis is the shortest?
questions.solution: The stages of nuclear division in mitosis are prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Prophase is the longest phase of mitosis while anaphase is the shortest phase. Anaphase is characterized by splitting of centromere and pulling of chromosomes towards the poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Splitting of the centromere is a significance feature of
questions.solution: During anaphase of mitosis and anaphase II of meiosis centromere splits and chromatids are separated, these chromatids are known as daughter chromosome and they start moving towards opposite poles. During anaphase I of meiosis, disjunction of chromosomal pair occurs and chromosomes are separated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is not correct about mitosis?
options: Usually restricted to the diploid cells and haploid cells of some social insects
Furrow extends centripetally and microfilament ring brings about cleavage in plant cells.
Growth in multicellular organisms is a result of Mitosis
questions.solution: Mitosis is an equational division in which one cell divides to form <math><mn>2</mn></math> daughter cells having the same number of chromosomes. It is quantitatively and qualitatively equational division. In animal cells, the cleavage furrow extends centripetally and the microfilament ring is involved in this process. In plant cells, the cell plate grows centrifugally without involving microfilaments.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the columns.
 
  Column-I   Column-II
(a) Leptotene (i) Chiasmata
(b) Zygotene (ii) Chromosomes visible
(c) Pachytene (iii) The pairing of homologous chromosome
(d) Diplotene (iv) Clear appearance of tetrads
questions.solution: In leptotene, condensation of chromosomes starts to form chromosomes; then in zygotene, homologous chromosomes come together to for pair known as synapsis. Crossing over or recombination occurs in pachytene and chiasmata becomes visible in diplotene.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Colchicine is a chemical that stops chromatids from separating during mitosis. If a cell is treated with colchicine, at which stage of mitosis will this cell reach but not complete?
questions.solution: Colchicine is a mitotic inhibitor. It does not allow spindle fibres to be formed. Thus, condensation of chromosomes will occur and prophase will be completed. But metaphase won't be completed. The metaphase stage is characterized by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The diagram shows the cell cycle. During which phase do chromosomes condense and become visible?
questions.solution: Interphase, therefore, consists of G1, S, and G2. During G1, cells make the RNA, enzymes, and other proteins needed for growth. At the end of G1, the cell becomes committed to dividing or not dividing. The nuclear division follows interphase, referred to as the M phase (M for mitosis). Growth stops temporarily during mitosis. Prophase which is the first stage of karyokinesis of mitosis follows the S and G2 phases of interphase. Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material. The chromosomal material becomes untangled during the process of chromatin condensation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select incorrect statements.

1. Diplotene stage is not recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
2. Recombination nodules contain a recombinase enzyme.
3. Interkinesis is generally short-lived.
4. In anaphase II separation of homologous chromosomes (bivalent) separate to opposite poles.
questions.solution: In the diplotene stage, the synaptonemal complex starts dissolution or disintegrating and the chromosomes start separating after crossing over. Recombination nodules contain a recombinase enzyme which helps in the process of recombination. Separation of homologous chromosomes (bivalent) occurs during anaphase I and this is known as disjunction, it results in a reduction in chromosome number to half. In anaphase II chromatids of a chromosome separate to opposite poles with the splitting the centromere taking place. Interkinesis is the resting stage between two meiotic divisions and generally short-lived.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
The following statements describe events during the mitotic cell cycle. What is the correct order of these events in the mitotic cell cycle?

I. Chromosomes migrate to opposite poles of the spindle.
II. Chromosomes arrange themselves at the equator of the spindle.
III. Chromosomes condense and the nuclear membrane disappears.
IV. Centromeres divide.
questions.solution: During mitosis, the chromosomes condense and nuclear membrane disappears at prophase. They are attached to spindle fibers and are brought to the equator at metaphase. Centromeres divide and one chromatid of each chromosome is pulled to opposite sides of the cell at anaphase. Chromosomes reach the poles, they decondense and form nuclear membrane at telophase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is not the incorrect sequence of prophase I of meiosis?
questions.solution: Prophase I of meiosis is of longest duration and is further subdivided into five sub phases: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, diakinesis. Leptotene shows bouquet formation. The pairing of homologous chromosome or synapsis occurs in zygotene. Crossing over occurs in pachytene. Chiasmata formation occurs in diplotene, and terminalisation occurs in diakinesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which character marks the beginning of the second phase of mitosis?
questions.solution: The nuclear membrane disintegrates at the end of prophase, and the disintegration of the nuclear membrane marks the beginning of metaphase. In metaphase, chromosome starts moving towards the centre of the cell and gets organized in one straight line to form metaphase plate. Spindle fibre attachés to the kinetochore of each chromosome from each pole.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following four statements (i-iv)

(i) Every chromosome essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere.

(ii) During different stages of cell division, cells show structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus.

(iii) Nuclear pores are the passages through which movement of RNA and protein takes place in one direction between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

(iv) Chromatin contains DNA, some basic proteins called histone and RNA only.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statements (i) and (ii) are correct. Nuclear pores are the passages through which the movement of RNA and proteins takes place in both directions between the nucleus and cytoplasm. Chromatin contains DNA, some basic proteins, histones, some acidic non-histone proteins and RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In many cases, the chromosomes do undergo some dispersion, they do not reach an extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus. This statement is related with ________
questions.solution: In telophase I, chromatin formation will not occur and many times the cell directly enters to meiosis II or prophase II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If an individual wants to view diakinesis, which of these would be suitable?
questions.solution: Flower buds are the reproductive structures that perform meiosis. Onion flower buds are commonly used to observe all the phases of meiosis with acetocarmine or acetoorcein staining method.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Two homologous chromosomes are depicted in the diagram given below. Crossing over occurs between chromatid 2 and chromatid 3 at the point as depicted.



The gametes produced as a result of this crossing over will be
questions.solution: Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during the pachytene phase of meiosis I. In this example, after crossing over, chromosome number 1 will have one chromatid with Ab and another chromatid with AB. Chromosome number 2 will have one chromatid with ab and another chromatid with aB. In anaphase 1, one of these chromosomes will go in one cell and the other will go in another cell. Then in anaphase 2, the centromere of these chromosomes will split leading to the formation of four cells one with Ab, the other with AB, the third with ab and the fourth with aB.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the incorrectly matched pair in the given options.
options: Crossing over - Sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
questions.solution: In the cell cycle process, S phase is a part of the interphase stage. In this phase, the DNA of the cell is duplicated marking the decision of the cell to enter divisional stage. Mitosis is one of the two cell-division processes where the outcome is two daughter cells who are identical to the parent cell. Since new cells formed as equal/same in every aspect, this division is also called as equational division. Meiosis is the other type of division where the daughter cells formed have half the genetic content of the parent cell (also called as reductional division since the chromosome number is reduced). Crossing over is a step observed in the prophase I of meiotic I division stage, where the non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange their genetic materials as homologous chromosomes have their genes in the same location compared with non-homologous chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Crossing over occurs between ________chromatid of _______chromosome.
questions.solution: Crossing over is the exchange of chromosomal segment between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. It occurs during pachytene of prophase-I of meiosis, and it results in recombination of genes, producing genetic variation. It is carried out by enzyme recombinase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following two features are present in meiosis but absent in mitosis?
options: Pairing of homologous chromosome and recombination between them
questions.solution: Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination or crossing over between genes occurs only in meiosis and is absent in mitosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: It has been found that the domestic horses have 64 chromosomes in their cell. Predict the number of chromosomes in the egg cell of a female horse.
questions.solution: Egg cells are a type of gametes that participates in the process of sexual reproduction. These cells are known to have half the chromosome content compared to other somatic cells. These cells are formed by undergoing meiotic divisions which reduce the chromosome set from diploid to haploid. Since, the diploid cell of the horse if having 64 chromosomes, then its egg cell (gametic cell) will have half that is 32 chromosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The below image summarises the cell cycle of a typical eukaryotic cell. Using the image as a reference, determine the activities occurring at the G1 phase of the cell cycle.
questions.solution: G<sub>1</sub> phase is part of the interphase in the cell cycle process of a eukaryotic cell. G<sub>1</sub> phase is the stage between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication (S phase). In the G<sub>1</sub> phase, the cell is found to be metabolically active and shows continuous growth. S or synthesis phase is where DNA synthesis or replication takes place in the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The division of centromere is absent in
questions.solution: During anaphase I, chromosomal pairs separate and chromosomes start moving towards opposite poles. This separation of chromosomal pair is called disjunction, and it results in reduction in the number of chromosomes to half.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: At the end of the G<sub>2</sub> phase, the number of chromosomes and the amount of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in a diploid cell, respectively, is
questions.solution: If a cell at <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> phase has <math><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></math> chromosome and <math><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A,</mi></math> then during <math><mi>S </mi><mi>p</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>e,</mi></math> <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> replication occurs but chromosome number remains unchanged. As a result, chromosome number remains <math><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> but the quantity of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> becomes <math><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many copies of each different DNA molecule will be found in a cell at the beginning of each of these stages of the mitotic cell cycle?
 
  G 2 of Interphase Prophase Cytokinesis
A 1 1 2
B 1 2 1
C 2 1 2
D 2 2 2
questions.solution: All the three stages mentioned occur after S-phase; thus, DNA is duplicated (DNA is twice in amount). Even though two nuclei have formed in the dividing cell, until the cytoplasm is completely divided, the single mother cell will have 2 copies of DNA. Once the cytokinesis has completed, each daughter cell will have a single copy of DNA. Hence, the answer is D.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the plant cell during cytokinesis, cell wall development starts from
options: peripheral and move towards centre of the cell
centre and move towards centre of the cell
centre and move towards peripheral of the cell
peripheral and move towards outside of the cell.
questions.solution: In plant cell cytokinesis occurs by cell plate formation which is formed by fragments of <math><mi>E</mi><mi>R</mi></math> , Golgi body and remains of spindle fibres known as phragmoplast. A small plate develops in the center which grows towards periphery thus touching the existing wall.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The photomicrographs show cells in various stages of the cell cycle. Identify the stage where semi-conservative replication of DNA takes place.
questions.solution: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time, the amount of DNA per cell doubles. Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material. The chromosomal material becomes untangled during the process of chromatin condensation. The metaphase is characterised by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres. At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously and the two daughter chromatids begin their migration towards the two opposite poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following four statements (I–IV) related to cell cycle, and select the correct option stating them as true [T] and false [F].

i. G1 phase is a metabolically active stage of the cell cycle.
ii. Interphase is the phase of actual cell division.
iii. The number of chromosomes doubles in S-phase.
iv. The cells that do not divide further exit the G1 - phase to enter a quiescent stage.
questions.solution: Interphase is the preparatory phase where the cell prepares itself for cell division by increasing the concentration of proteins. Replication of chromosomes takes place in the S phase where the number of chromatids double.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sister chromatids of a chromosome have:
options: Different genes at the same locus
Different alleles at the same gene at the same locus
Same alleles of the same gene at the same locus
questions.solution: Sister chromatids of a chromosome are formed as a result of DNA replication during the S phase of interphase. Thus, sister chromatids consist of the same alleles of the same gene at the same locus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Analyze the statements and select the correct option.
 
a) The cell cycle gets completed in G1–S–G2–M phase. 
b) G1 phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. 
c) In the G1 phase, the cell is metabolically active and DNA replicates.
questions.solution:
In mitosis, the cell cycle consists of long interphase followed by a short mitotic or M-phase. Interphase is the phase between two successive cell divisions. It is a metabolically very active phase because of the biosynthesis of a number of molecules. It is divided into G1, S and G2 phases/sub-stages. The M phase starts with the nuclear division, corresponding to the separation of daughter chromosomes (karyokinesis) and usually ends with the division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis). G1 phase is also called the growth phase or post-mitotic phase.

G1 phase is the longest phase of interphase; the maximum increase in the cell size occurs during this phase. In this phase, there is an active synthesis of RNA and proteins. G1 phase is the interval between the M and S phases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In meiosis the actual haploidy in terms of DNA comes in
questions.solution: In anaphase II, the sister chromatids separate and move towards opposite poles of the spindle. This ensures the haploidy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If the egg of sexually reproducing organisms contains 16 chromosomes, what will be the number of dyads in a<math><mtext>naphase I?</mtext></math>
questions.solution: Egg contains a haploid number of chromosomes; thus, the diploid number will be 32 in the oocyte. In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes segregate in the form of a dyad; thus, the number of dyads will be 32.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Meiosis is one of the two cell division process observed to occur in cells. Which statement from below correctly describes the outcome of a successful meiotic division?
options: Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Two daughter cells are produced Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
Two daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
questions.solution:
Meiotic division is a type of cell division where two cell division occurs with only one round of DNA duplication process. The eventual new cells that are formed have half the genetic content of the participating cells. If a participating cell has 20 chromosome, its eventual daughter cell will have 10 chromosome. Thus, the statement of each daughter cell having one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell is the correct one.

Mitosis is another type of cell division process where the DNA duplication occurs once and the cell also divides one time. The resulting daughter cells formed have the same amount of genetic content as the parent cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the option regarding this diagrammatic representation.
questions.solution: Anaphase is the shortest phase of the mitotic cell division part of the cell cycle. In this phase, the centrally aligned sister chromatids spilt at the centromere and move towards to the opposite pole.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In meiosis, haploid cells are formed. During this process, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus disappear
questions.solution: In meiosis, karyokinesis takes place twice; therefore, nuclear membrane and nucleolus disappear 2 times (in prophase-I and prophase-II) and reappear (in telophase-I and telophase-II).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many times meiosis will take place for the formation of 80 wheat grains?
questions.solution:
For the formation of a single wheat grain we require:
80 egg cell and 80 pollen grain. Usually, a single functional egg cell is formed at the end of meiosis. Therefore, for the formation of  80 egg cell, there should be 80 meiotic division.
Single meiotic division in microspore mother cell produces 4 functional pollen grain. Thus produce 80 pollen grain the total number of meiotic division would be 20.
Therefore, in all, there will be 100 meiotic division 80 for egg cell and 20 division for pollen grain to produce 80 wheat grain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plant cell undergoes cell division to form two new cell. The below diagram represents a certain stage of the cell cycle of plant cells. Determine the step/stage of the cell cycle process that will happen just before the represented process starts.
questions.solution:
Cell division phase of cell cycle has two stages - karyokinesis and cytokinesis. Karyokinesis deals with nuclear division where at the end of this stage two nuclei are formed. Following karyokinesis, cytokinesis occurs where the cytoplasm is divided in two resulting in formation of two new whole individual cells. The given diagram represent the cytokinesis stage of plant cell division. In it, the division occurs by making a cell plate in the cytoplasm between the two newly formed nuclei which later becomes the cell wall of the new cell that will form.

Diakinesis is part of prophase I of meiosis I which is part of karyokinesis.

DNA synthesis is part of S -phase in interphase.

Interphase is the stage of cell cycle that occurs between two cell division processes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the process of meiosis, there are two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division. How many cycles of DNA replication are required in meiosis?
questions.solution: Meiosis is a type of cell division in which the number of chromosomes in the daughter cell is reduced by half. DNA replication occurs during S phase. This is followed by meiosis I (reduction division) and meiosis II (equational division). There is no DNA replication between the two meiotic divisions. Hence, DNA replication occurs only once.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the cell division events happening in these mammalian cells.
options: a- Meiotic metaphase I, b- Mitotic Anaphase, c- Meiotic Anaphase II
a- Mitotic Metaphase, b- Mitotic Anaphase, c- Meiotic Anaphase II
a- Mitotic Metaphase, b- Mitotic Anaphase c- Meiotic Anaphase I
a- Meiotic Metaphase II b- Meiotic Anaphase I c- Meotic Anaphase II
questions.solution: In meiosis, there is a reduction in cell division and that occurs in gametes. This organism has 2n = 6 chromosomes and during meiosis, they will be reduced to 3 chromosomes. In diagram (a) Three homologous pairs of chromosomes are in line along with the metaphase plate during metaphase l, followed by which, the homologous chromosome will separate and the cell will enter meiosis ll. In diagram (b), which is mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids of chromosomes move apart. In diagram (c), which is anaphase ll, sister chromatids of chromosomes move apart. In mitosis, chromosome number remains the same; hence, the number of chromosomes will be six.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many centromeres are present in a bivalent and how many bivalents are present in a diploid cell of human females respectively?
questions.solution: Diploid cell of human consists of 46 chromosomes, thus during meiosis it forms 23 bivalents. Bivalents are pair of homologous chromosomes formed during zygotene of meiosis. Each chromosome consists of one centromere, a bivalent consists of two chromosome thus it consists of two centromere.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A typical process of cell division in a human cell approximately lasts for
questions.solution: In a human eukaryotic cell the whole cell cycle process takes place in about 24 hours. The interphase consumes around 23 hours of the total duration of the cycle. The whole cell division stage is quite fast and short lasting about one hour only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the meiotic division, at which stage the homologous chromosomes separate without the sister chromatids breaking apart?
questions.solution: Meiosis is a reductional division process where the cell undergoes two successive division processes to reduce chromosome number to half. It is divided into meiotic stage I and II. Anaphase I is part of the meiotic stage I, where the sister chromatids separate from its homologous counterpart. The chromatids centromere remains intact in this stage and do not separate. Their separation occurs in anaphase II in meiotic stage II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A cell divides when its karyocytoplasmic index or karyoplasmic index
questions.solution: Karyoplasmic index is the ratio of the volume of the nucleus to the volume of the cytoplasm. For each cell fixed volume of nucleus can control the fixed volume of cytoplasm, when the volume of the cytoplasm increases more than the volume of the nucleus the karyoplasmic index decreases. Thus the cell starts dividing.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the given options, which one is a characteristic feature of the zygotene stage of prophase-I observed in meiosis?
questions.solution: Zygotene stage is observed in prophase-I of meiosis-I divisional phase. In this stage, chromosomes start pairing together forming an association called synapsis. This pairing is observed between homologous chromosomes. This synapsis results in formation of a complex structure called synaptonemal complex. Crossing over is observed in pachytene stage of prophase-I, where exchange of genetic materials occurs. In diakinesis, the paired of chromosomes separate resulting in terminalisation of chiasmata. Chiasmata is formed when the chromosomes of synaptonemal complex separate from each other. Chromomeres are linearly arranged chromatin granules observed on chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The nucleus of a gamete of an animal has 5 pg DNA. What will be the content of DNA in the somatic cell of the same animal at the end on G2 phase?
questions.solution: Egg is a gametic cell having half the genetic content that is 5pg DNA (haploid). Thus, the diploid state of cell will have 10pg DNA. During the interphase, G2 phase occurs after the S phase (DNA duplication). The genetic content of cell in G2 phase will be double of the diploid state - 20pg.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mitosis occurs in
options: Both haploid individuals and diploid individuals
questions.solution:
Somatic cells of a multicellular organism arise from a single cell by mitotic divisions. Body growth of a multicellular organism and replacement of its lost cells is accomplished through mitosis.

Animals undergo "open" mitosis, where the nuclear envelope breaks down before the chromosomes separate, while fungi undergo "closed" mitosis, where chromosomes divide within an intact cell nucleus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these pairs are incorrectly clubbed together?
options: Cells in adult animals which do not divide - Heart cells
Disc shaped structures at the surface of centromere -  Kinetochores
Initiation of assembly of mitotic spindle - Mitotic metaphase
questions.solution: Heart cells on differentiation lose the ability to divide in adulthood. Mitosis is the cell division process where the cell divides to form two identical daughter cells to its parent cell. Kinetochores are present over the centromeres that held the sister chromatids together. Kinetochores are disc shaped. The mitotic spindle apparatus forms during the prophase of mitosis and in metaphase the chromosomes move towards the equator.

questions.solution: During prophase, nucleolus and nuclear membrane disappear, chromosomes and occurs after G<sub>2</sub> interphase. In metaphase, the chromosomes are arranged at the equator of the cell and this phase acts as a checkpoint of mitosis. Centromere splits and chromatids are separated during anaphase and daughter chromosomes start moving towards the opposite poles with chromosomal disjunction. Nuclear membrane, nucleolus and ER reappears during telophase, thus two nuclei are formed, which is followed by cytokinesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct even from below that is most likely to occur during the three subphases of the interphase of the mitotic cell cycle.
options: During G<sub>1</sub> phase, the cell is metabolically active and replicates its DNA.
During S phase, duplication of centrioles takes place.
The number of chromosomes becomes double in the synthesis phase.
Replication of DNA starts during the G<sub>2</sub> phase and proteins are synthesized in order to prepare the cell for mitosis.
questions.solution:
Interphase can be subdivided into 3 further phase: G1, S and G2.
G1 phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During G1 phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Anaphase I - Homologous chromosomes are separated
Metaphase I - Pairing of maternal and paternal homologous chromosomes takes place
Interphase - A nuclear envelope encloses each haploid set of chromosomes
Prophase I - Non-homologous chromosomes are separated
questions.solution:
Anaphase I involves separartion of homologous chromosomes which start moving opposite poles so each tetrad is divided into two daughter dyads.

In Metaphase I Centromeres of homologous chromosomes lie equisdistant from equator and are directed towards the poles while arms generally lie horizontally on the equator. Each homologous chromosome has two kinetochores and both the kinetochores of a chromosome are joined to the chromosomal or tractile fibre of same side.

Whereas Prophase I is divided in five subphases i.e., leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.

Interphase : It is the period between the end of one cell division to the beginning of next cell division. It is also called resting phase or not dividing phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A bacterium divides every 35 minutes. If a culture containing 10<sup>5</sup> cells per ml is grown for 175 minutes, what will be the cell concentration per ml after 175 minutes?
questions.solution:
The 'n', the time difference is 175/35 = 5 minutes, then, 2n = 25 = 32. 
The culture initially had 105 cells/ml, therefore, 32 X 105 cells will be present after 175 minutes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the circled phase of cell division.
questions.solution: The first phase of mitotic division is prophase. During prophase, the chromatin undergoes condensation to form chromosomes, the nuclear envelope breaks down, the centrioles near the nucleus begin to separate and move to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Meiosis and mitosis are found to be the two types of cell division. A cell is observed to have 50 chromosomes in its nucleus during interphase before entering S-phase. How many chromosomes will it have after undergoing division by the two-division process?
 
  Meiosis Mitosis
1 100 25
2 50 50
3 50 100
4 25 50
questions.solution: Meiosis is a type of reductional division process where the chromosome number is halved in the daughter cell compared to its parent cell. It is significant in the process of reproduction for making gametes. Mitosis is a type of cell division where the chromosome number between parent cell and daughter cell remains the same. It is also called as equational division. Therefore, if parent cell has 50 chromosomes then after mitosis the daughter cell will have 50 chromosomes as well but after meiosis, the daughter cell formed will have 25 chromosomes only. Thus, row 4th is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding diploid cell and identify the INCORRECT one.

II. It can undergo a mitotic division to repair a cell.
III. It can undergo a reduction division to form haploid cells.
IV. It is the one that possesses two complete sets of chromosomes.
questions.solution: A cell having two sets of chromosomes is termed as diploid cell (statement IV) which produces haploid cell via meiosis (Statement III). Meiosis is the reductional division process where the chromosome number is halved in the newly formed daughter cells.  Mitosis (equational division) usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. The growth of multicellular organisms is due to mitosis. Mitosis produces genetically identical daughter cells. It is not useful in repair of single cell rather useful in repair of tissue by replacing the damaged cells. Hence, statement II is not correct.

questions.solution: Cell cycle consists of interphase and M - Phase. Interphase consists of G1 phase, S phase and G2 phase. G1 phase is Gap1 phase in which max growth and protein synthesis occurs. S phase is synthesis phase in which DNA replication occurs and G2 phase in which synthesis of tubulin protein occurs. M- phase consists of Karyokinesis or division of nucleus and cytokinesis or division of cytoplasm.

questions.solution:
The chromosomes become arranged on the metaphase plate, much as the chromosomes do in mitosis, and are attached to the now fully formed spindle. In metaphase II, the centromeres contain two kinetochores that attach to spindle fibers from the centrosomes at opposite poles. The new equatorial metaphase plate is rotated by 90 degrees when compared to meiosis I, perpendicular to the previous plate.
Disjunction of chromosomes takes place in anaphase-I and II when chromosomes move to the opposite poles of the cell.

Plectonemic coiling refers to inter-twining of a double helix DNA molecule in such a way that for its correction unwinding of DNA helix molecule is required, this take place in mitosis in which sister chromatids are tightly coiled upon each other. In the zygotene stage, homologs login to synapse by coming to approximate alignment.

questions.solution: Cell growth during cell division is a continuous process and occurs through cell cycle, but interphase is the metabolically the most active phase. The cell cycle is a genetically controlled process. Synthesis of organelle occurs during the G1 phase and DNA replication occurs only during S-phase of the cell cycle.

questions.solution: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally, as needed to replace cells that have been lost because of injury or cell death. These cells that do not divide further exit G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G0 ) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution:
The cell cycle is controlled by the enzymes like cyclin-dependent kinases (Cdks). In eukaryotes, multiple cyclins are present and each of which acts during a specific checkpoint in cell cycle regulation. Common classes of cyclins includes
  • G1-phase cyclins 
  • G1/S-phase cyclins
  • S-phase cyclins
  • M-phase cyclins
M-phase cyclins form M-CDK complexes and drive the cell's entry into mitosis and acts on the anaphase-promoting complex.

questions.solution: Zygotene is the second stage of Prophase I where the chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis and the paired chromosomes are known as homologous chromosomes. Pachytene is the stage where bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads and is characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules which function as the sites of crossing over between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes and is mediated by the enzyme called recombinase. The stage where sister chromatids remain associated but homologous chromosomes separate is called Anaphase I. During Anaphase II the sister chromatids move towards the opposite poles of the cell due to the simultaneous splitting of the centromere.

questions.solution: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: A. Inter phase B. M Phase (Mitosis phase). These type of cells do not proceed further in the cell cycle and exit the G1 phase to enter into a stage of inactivity known as the quiescent stage or Go phase. In this stage the cells remain metabolically active but do not proliferate unless and until there is need. questions.solution: The Prophase I of  Meosis I is further divide into 5 phases - Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. In the leptotene stage the compaction of chromosomes is continued and they become more visible under light microscope. Second stage is zygotene where chromosomes start pairing together and the process is called synapsis.  These paired chromosomes are called homologous chromosomes. In the next phase of pachytene these bilvalent chromosomes now appear as tetrads. Pachytene is also characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules which is the site for non sister chromatids to cross over. During the start of diplotene phase there is dissolution of synaptonemal complex and the homologous chromosomes separate from each other except at the sites where crossover has taken place and form an X shaped structure known as chiasmata. The final phase of diakinesis is where terminalisation of chiasmata takes place.

questions.solution: Segregation of Mendelian factor (Aa) occurs during Anaphase I. The paired homologous chromosomes separate during anaphase I in meiosis I so that each gamete receives only one chromosomes of each homologous pair. This disjunction of chromosomal pair leads to segregation of Mendelian factors present on them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During which phase of cell cycle amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as <math><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>?
questions.solution: Cell cycle consists of interphase and mitotic (M) phase. Interphase is divided into <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> stages. The mitotic phase is the actual division phase and is divided into karyokinesis and cytokinesis. DNA is seen in all phases. In the M phase both 4C and 2C of DNA is seen. In S phase the synthesis of DNA takes place and hence the amount of DNA doubles. Thus after S phase in G2 phase the DNA doubles i.e. it becomes 4C.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During meiosis, a microspore mother cell has 12 bivalents, the number of chromosomes in its pollen grains will be:
questions.solution:
Meiosis is a reductional type of division where the chromosome numbers are halved in the daughter cells formed. During the meiotic division process, there is formation of bivalents which are paired homologous chromosomes. If cell has 12 bivalents, then the mother cell will have 24 chromosomes.

Pollen grains are formed from each of the daughter cell formed after a complete meiotic process of a microspore mother cell. Thus, the chromosomes in pollen grain will be half of the mother cell which is 12.

Chromosomes are arranged along the equator during prophase
Chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids at anaphase of mitosis.
A cell plate is laid down during interphase
questions.solution: Mitosis consists of karyokinesis followed by cytokinesis. Karyokinesis includes prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. In prophase, the condensation of chromatin takes place. In metaphase nuclear envelope disintegrates and chromosome condensation completes and chromosomes align at the equator. In anaphase, the chromosomes split and two chromatids separate and thus they start migrating towards the poles. At telophase the chromatids reach the end.

questions.solution:
Prophase - I

- It is subdivided into 5 phases :

A. Leptotene (Lepto = thin or delicate)

B. Zygotene (Zygo = related to pairing or joining)

- Synapsis or pairing of chromosomes occur to bring the homologous chromosomes together.

- Synapsis is followed by the formation of synaptonemal complex (or bivalent or tetrad).

C. Pachytene (Pachy = thick)

- Starting of diplotene is characterized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the

separation of the homologous chromosomes from each other except at the X shaped sites of cross

over. These X shapes sites are termed as Chiasmata.

E. Diakinesis (= Movement or separation of both)

- It is characterized by the terminalization of chiasmata.

questions.solution: Cytokinesis is the final step in cell division. Cleavage furrow forms at the equatorial cortex after anaphase. This furrow advances inwards to separate the two daughter cells. Furrow formation is done by actin-myosin filaments within the equatorial region to form cleavage during early anaphase.  Various organelles are distributed between the newly formed two daughter cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sister chromatids are found in
questions.solution: During metaphase, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope. This is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied. At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere. Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell. This occurs in mitotic as well as meiotic metaphase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Second check point of cell cycle lies between
questions.solution:
Checkpoints are internal controlling mechanisms in the cell cycle. Due to these checkpoints, the cell cycle is monitored at various stages. There are three major checkpoints seen. The first is as the G1 phase ends. Second is when G2 ends and the cell is about to enter the Mitotic phase. The third is during the metaphase.

The first checkpoint checks whether the conditions are suitable for cell division to place or not. If the conditions are not proper the cell will be arrested and will enter the G0 phase instead of the G2 phase. The second checkpoint is at G2-M interphase. Before the cell enters the M phase the cell is checked at this point. This ensures whether all the chromosomes in the cell are duplicated or not. It also checks that the DNA which is replicated is not damaged. The third checkpoint is at the end of Metaphase and this is also known as spindle checkpoint as it checks whether all the chromatids are connected to spindle fibres or not.

Number of chromatids in P = 8, Number of chromosomes in G<sub>2</sub> = 4

questions.solution:
Somatic cells undergo mitotic cell division so, there is no reduction division and chromosome number remain the same. At the beginning of mitosis, there are 4 chromosomes, and each chromosome replicates during S phase and form sister chromatids. So the number of chromosomes is 4, and chromatids are 4 x 2 = 8. Hence, during G1 phase
Chromatids number - 4
Chromosomes number- 4
During S phase
Chromatids number - 8
Chromosome number – 4
During the G2 phase
Chromatids number - 8
Chromosomes number - 4

Meiosis is a process which takes place in sex cells (sperms/eggs) where a single cell divides twice to produce four cells containing half the original amount of genetic information.

Anaphase I is a part of meiosis I, first cell division that separates the duplicated genetic material carried in the nucleus of a parent cell into two identical daughter cells. The separated chromosomes are pulled by the spindle fibres to opposite poles of the cell.

In prometaphase around the centromere, there is a protein develop that is called the kinetochore. Each chromosome gets attached to the spindle by its centromere in the center and lines up all the chromosomes in one plane in the equator. It is followed by the third phase of mitosis i.e. metaphase. In anaphase, centromeres divide and in telophase chromosomes are pulled apart to poles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following stage is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata?
questions.solution: The first phase of Meiosis I is prophase I. It is further divided into five phases. 1) Leptotene: condensation of chromatin material takes place in this stage 2) Zygotene: The homologous chromosome formation is seen in this stage. This is known as synapsis and this is also facilitated by the formation of synaptonemal complex. 3) Pachytene: At this point, a tetrad of chromosomes is formed and this is known as bivalent. Crossing over is also seen in this stage. 4) Diplotene: The synaptonemal complex degrades and chiasmata formation is seen. 5) Diakinesis: This is the final stage of prophase. Here the chromosomes condense further. Four proper tetrads are visible. During this stage, terminalization is seen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Colchicine is obtained from
questions.solution:
Colchicine is a type of alkaloid that many applications. One of the major applications is in the treatment of diseases gout and Behcet's disease. It is also useful in the plant breeding process where it induces polyploidy by inhibiting the segregation of the chromosomes during meiosis resulting in half of the gametes with whole chromosomes and another half with no chromosomes.

Colchicine is produced by the flowering plant Colchicum autumnale. The alkaloid is obtained from the bulb-like corms formed in the plant. This plant is considered deadly poisonous due to its colchicine content.
