<math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mo>)</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">v</mi><mo>)</mo></math>
questions.solution:
Cell division is the phase in the cell cycle where the cell divides to form new daughter cells. Depending on the type of division - Mitosis - makes two new identical daughter cells and Meiosis - makes four new daughter cells with half the genetic content of the mother cell.

During the mitotic cell division, cell undergoes through stages of division ultimately dividing to form two new cells-

Prophase - It is the first stage of nuclear division and marked by condensation of chromosomal material. Centrosomes start moving towards to the opposite poles. Each of the centrosome radiate microtubules called spindle fibres that hold the chromosomes at centromere. The radiating centrosome looks like a start hence called as aster. Both centrosome and the spindle fibres are called as mitotic apparatus.

Metaphase - In this stage the nuclear envelope disintegrated completely and disappears. The condensation of the chromosome is complete. The condensed chromosomes start moving and arranging towards the equatorial plane with support from spindle fibres that bind to the kinetochore of centromere in each chromosome.

Anaphase - It is the shortest phase of the nuclear division. In this phase, each chromosome split and move away from equator towards to the poles. The sister chromatids separate and show various shapes of the chromatids like V, I, L and J shaped.

Telophase - The last phase of nuclear division where the separated chromosomes cluster at the poles. The nuclear envelope reappears with decrease in cytoplasmic viscosity. Nucleolus, Golgi complex along with endoplasmic reticulum are reformed.

Cytokinesis - The last stage of cell division process. Once the nuclear content has been divided and separated in the karyokinesis process, the whole cell then divides to form new daughter cells by separation of the protoplast.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A which stage of meiosis does the genetic constituent of gametes is finally decided?
questions.solution: When each daughter cell gets a half number of the chromosome from a parent cell through which the genetic constituent of gametes is finally decided. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the total number of the correct statement:

I. Cell-plate formation occurs in plant cell during cytokinesis.
II. During cytokinesis mitochondria and plastid gets distributed between two daughter cells in mitosis.
III. Liquid endosperm in coconut is syncytium.
IV. Furrow formation occurs in the animal cell during cytokinesis.
questions.solution: In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane. The furrow gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre dividing the cell cytoplasm into two. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells. In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The number of mitotic division that must occur in a cell of the root tip to form 256 cells is
questions.solution:
Mitosis is a type of cell division where two identical daughter cells are formed. This cell division process occurs in certain steps. The chromosome number between parent cell and daughter cell remains the same. It is also called as equational division.

Each division of a single cell forms two new cell. Thus, if 'n' number of mitotic divisions are taking place then the total number of cells formed will be 2n

Root tip cells divide mitotically to give 256, thus, number of divisions required will be 2n = 256=28. n = 8 .

Number of division is equal to the number of generations.

options: It replaces old or worn out cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many meiotic divisions are required to produce 104 male gametes in a typical Angiospermic plant?
questions.solution:
Gametes are produced via meiotic cell division process. Each microspore mother cell of sporogenous tissue of microsporangium divides mitotically to produce 4 pollen grains. Each pollen grain contains two cells, generative cell and vegetative cell. The generative cell divides to form two male gametes. Thus, each meiotic division of microspore mother cell produces 8 male gametes.

For producing 104 male gametes, 13 meiotic divisions are required.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During which phase of the cell cycle the amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?
questions.solution:
The sequential events that lead to formation of the new daughters by cell division and preceded by duplication of its genome is termed as cell cycle. Whole cell cycle is broadly divided into two parts -interphase and divisional phase. The interphase is divided into -

G1 phase - The cell grows and develops by been metabolically active but does not duplicate the genetic content.

S phase - In the synthesis phase, DNA duplication occurs. The genetic content is doubled in this phase. There is no increase in the chromosome number as such.

G2 phase - This phase follows S phase having double the genomic content. During this phase, all proteins required for the divisional process is synthesized and the growth of cell continues.

G0 phase - Some cells lose the ability to divide further into new cells. Such cells after G1 phase enter the G0 or quiescent stage of cell cycle.

After interphase, the cell enters the divisional phase which is symbolized as M phase for mitosis. The cell in divisional phase undergoes nuclear division, where the duplicated DNA content is separated into two new nuclei and then the whole cell divides to form new daughter cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many chromosomes will the cell have at G1, after S, and after M-phase respectively, if it has 21 chromosomes at interphase?
questions.solution: If an interphase cell has 22 chromosomes than the cell at G1 has 22 chromosomes. In S phase on duplication of DNA occurs but chromosome number remains unchanged, thus cell at S phase will also have 22 chromosomes. After the M - phase or mitosis phase equal division occurs and two identical cells are produced having 22 chromosomes each.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A somatic cell that has just completed the S-phase of its cell cycle, as compared to gamete of the same species has
options: twice the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
the same number of chromosomes but twice the amount of DNA
twice the number of chromosomes and four times the amount of DNA
four times the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA
questions.solution: The S phase is interphase where synthesis or replication of DNA takes place. During this phase, the chromosome number remains unchanged while the DNA in each cell doubles. Diploid somatic cells will therefore have twice the number of chromosomes and four times the number of DNA (2n) after the S phase as compared to the gametes which are haploid in number (n).

options: Homologous chromosomes pair and form bivalents
questions.solution: Mitosis is equational division in which two chromatids of a chromosome separates during anaphase. Chromosomes align at the equator during metaphase and 2 spindle fibre attaches to each chromosome. During anaphase, the kinetochore are pulled apart and centromere splits and chromatids are separated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify CORRECTLY matched pair.
options: Diakinesis-Recombination of non sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes
questions.solution:
Meiosis is divided into two stages of division - Meiosis I and II. Of the two stages, meiosis II is similar to mitosis division phase. Meiosis I is involved in the paring and recombination of the homologous chromosomes.

Zygotene stage is observed in prophase-I of meiosis-I divisional phase. In this stage chromosomes start pairing together forming an association called synapsis. This pairing is observed between homologous chromosomes. This synapsis results in formation of a complex structure called synaptonemal complex.

Crossing over is observed in pachytene stage of prophase-I where exchange of genetic materials occurs. In diakinesis the paired of chromosomes separate resulting in terminalisation of chiasmata.

Diplotene stage is marked by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and separation of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sequentially, the last stage to occur among the following is:
questions.solution: The meotic Prophase I consists of five stages namely - Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis. During the leptotene stage the compaction of chromosomes continues and they become more visible under light microscope. In second stage chromosomes start pairing together to form homologous chromosomes through the process of synapsis. During pachytene these bilvalent chromosomes now appear as tetrads and recombination nodules also appear. During the start of diplotene phase there is dissolution of synaptonemal complex and the homologous chromosomes separate from each other except at the sites where crossover has taken place and forming an X shaped structure known as chiasmata. The final phase is diakinesis where terminalisation of chiasmata takes place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A teacher was trying to show the different stages of a type of cell division to the students. At a particular stage, it was observed that the chromosomes were separating but there was no splitting of centromeres. This stage would be
questions.solution: Meiosis is a reductional division process where the cell undergoes two successive division processes to reduce chromosome number to half. It is divided into the meiotic stages I and II. Anaphase I is part of the meiotic stage I, where the sister chromatids separate from its homologous counterpart. The chromatids centromere remains intact in this stage and do not separate. Their separation occurs in anaphase II in meiotic stage II.

S Phase or Synthesis phase-

questions.subject: Botany

options: In this phase, cell is metabolically active and grows continuously.
It involves replication of RNA, DNA and proteins.
The cell has an option to stop cell cycle and undergo differentiation.
questions.solution: Interphase is the first growth stage after cell division. Three stages occur during interphase i.e.G1, S, and G2 stage wherein G1 stage cells mature by making more cytoplasm and cell organelles. S phase is called the post-mitotic gap phase and during that phase, the cell synthesizes enzyme and energy needed for DNA duplication. It occurs between the G1 and G2 phases of the interphase. In the G2 phase, all cell structures needed for cell division are made. Example: centriole. So the incorrect option is B.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not true about the S phase?
options: Amount of DNA per cell become half
Even after S phase chromosome number become double
questions.solution:
S-phase (synthesis phase) is the part of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, occurring between the G1 phase and the G2 phase. It is characterized by: DNA and histones are synthesized and DNA content gets doubled. DNA replicates in a semi-conservative manner. 

The amount of DNA per cell becomes double even after S phase chromosome number remains the same.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In prophase I, the stage that closely resembles prometaphase of mitosis is:
questions.solution: The final stage of meiotic prophase I is diakinesis. This is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata. During this phase the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down. Diakinesis represents transition to metaphase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The minimum number of chiasmata in a bivalent is/are
questions.solution: Chiasmata is the point of contact or the X shaped structure formed between two non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosome during the process of crossing over of genetic material. A bivalent is a pair of the homologous chromosome that has exchanged DNA in at least one site called the chiasmata. The minimum chiasmata found in a bivalent is one and can go up to three in rare cases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements are true?
options: In animal cells during S phase DNA replication begins in nucleus and centriole duplication in cytoplasm
During G1 phase protein are synthesized and cell continues to grow
All cells in adult animals appear to exhibit cell division
questions.solution: During the G2 phase protein is synthesized and the cell continues to grow. Some cells for example the heart cells in adult animals do not appear to exhibit cell division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following holds true for the pachytene stage of meiotic cell division?
options: This stage leads to genetic recombination, hence variations in sexually reproducing organisms.
In this stage, the process of exchange of genetic material between sister chromatids of non-  homologous chromosomes takes place.
This stage takes place only in haploid cells of the body eg. Gametes
questions.solution:
The meiotic cell division comprises two successive nuclear division the meiosis I and meiosis II. The meiosis I have four stages prophase I, metaphase 1, anaphase 1, and telophase 1. The prophase I have further been divided into five phases depending on the chromosomal behavior.

The pachytene is the third phase of the five phases where the four chromatids appear as tetrads. Crossing over between two homologous chromosomes takes place during this phase and therefore leads to the recombination of the genetic material on the two chromosomes. In this phase the exchange of genetic material between sister chromatids of non- homologous chromosomes takes place. The variations in sexually reproducing organisms are the result of this genetic recombination.

options:

No. of chromatids No. of chromosomes
G2 4 4

No. of chromatids No. of chromosomes

questions.solution: Somatic cells are those cells whose genes will not be passed onto future generations. Somatic cells are diploid in nature. In mitosis the nucleus of the cell divides and forms two nuclei with identical genetic information. Mitosis is completed in the following stages i.e. Prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. Prophase is the first phase of mitosis in which chromosome condenses and the nuclear envelope disappears. A chromosome consists of a single double-stranded DNA molecule while chromatids are two molecules of double-stranded DNA that joined together in the center by a centromere. So if no. of chromosomes in somatic cells is 4 then no.of chromatids will be 8.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When the number of chromosomes is already reduced to half in the first reduction division of meiosis. What is the necessity of the second mitotic division?
options: The division is required for the formation of four gametes.
The division ensures equal distribution of genes on the chromosomes.
The division ensures equal distribution of haploid chromosomes.
The division is required for segregation of replicated chromosomes.
questions.solution: There are two stages in the meiotic division, meiosis I and meiosis II. These stages mainly involve the reductional and equational division of the cells. In the first meiotic division, the chromosome number is reduced to half (haploid condition) and the chromatids move to the opposite poles. In the second meiotic division which resembles normal mitosis, there is the formation of four gametes and the chromosomes are distributed to each gamete, therefore the second meiotic division is required for the segregation of the replicated chromosome.

questions.q:
From the following, identify the two correct statements with reference to meiosis.

I. Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II but only a single cycle of DNA replication.
II. Development of chiasmata occurs in diakinesis.
III. Separation of two basic sets of chromosomes.
IV. No division of centromere.
questions.solution:
The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures, are called chiasmata.

Anaphase II: It begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome (which was holding the sister chromatids together), allowing them to move toward opposite poles of the cell by shortening of microtubules attached to kinetochores.

In metaphase II the centromere of the individual chromosome is attached to the two kinetochore-microtubules from either side and chromosomes are arranged in the center. In Anaphase II splitting of the centromere of each chromosome and in prophase II nuclear membranes disappear. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which phase of the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell remains constant at 4C level, considering that the initial amount of DNA was 2C?
questions.solution: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time, the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C, then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math><sub> </sub>phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis, while cell growth continues.

questions.solution: Exchange of segments between homologous chromosomes is known as crossing over. It occurs during pachytene stage of prophase-I of meiosis.

questions.solution: There are three types of cell divisions namely amitosis, mitosis, and meiosis. In amitosis, the chromosomes do not become visible. It is found in primitive life forms such as amoeba, bacteria, etc. The nucleus elongates in a dumb-bell shape and is followed by the invagination of the plasmalemma. The constriction in the nucleus, as well as plasmalemma, deepens and divide one amoeba into two daughter amoebae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these statements is not true?
options: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes.
The enzyme which is involved during crossing over is called recombinase.
Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of diakinesis.
Synaptonemal complex is formed during zygotene.
questions.solution: The first two stages of prophase I are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage that is pachytene. During this stage bivalent chromosomes now clearly appears as tetrads. This stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is also an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase. Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes. Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene, leaving the chromosomes linked at the sites of crossing over.

The <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> is the growth phase followed by the Synthesis phase and then the Gap phase where the cell is preparing itself for division and protein synthesis takes place after which the cell is ready to undergo mitosis. It is in the gap phase that the microtubules are assembled and later used for the mobilization of the chromosomes in the M phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following structures will be seen in metaphase-I of meiosis-I, in a plant cell that has 64 chromosomes?
questions.solution: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad. So if the total number of chromosomes is '2n', then the number of the bivalents will be half, i.e., 'n'. Hence, a plant cell having 64 chromosomes, will have 32 bivalents in the stage of Metaphase-I of Meiosis-I.
